name: Peter Higgs
description: Peter Higgs predicted the existence of a fundamental scalar boson — now called the Higgs boson — in 1964, a mechanism responsible for giving mass to elementary particles within the Standard Model of particle physics. His landmark paper proposed the spontaneous symmetry breaking mechanism that underpins electroweak unification. Nearly five decades after the prediction, the ATLAS and CMS experiments at CERN's Large Hadron Collider announced the boson's discovery in 2012, leading to Higgs sharing the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2013 with François Englert. Despite a modest publication record, Higgs's theoretical contribution is considered one of the most consequential in twentieth-century physics. His work has no direct industry ties, but underpins the entire enterprise of high-energy particle physics instrumentation.
